title: Daily giving

segments.voice: Wird: a daily portion, small enough to keep, and a verse that says what is easy twice. My portion. Today, a portion that leaves your hands.
screen: `MY PORTION.` → `A PORTION THAT LEAVES YOUR HANDS.`

segments.voice: A round-up button at checkout, a tip jar by the register, a coworker's fundraiser link: small giving is everywhere now. Amira's family has an older version. Her dad Yusuf keeps a jar by the coffee machine and drops something in every morning before he unlocks the door. Amira, broke until payday, says her food pantry shift should count instead. Yusuf says sadaqah means money, even a little. Two real views. Both have hadith behind them.
screen: `ROUND UP AT CHECKOUT.` → `A JAR BY THE COFFEE MACHINE.` → `DOES IT HAVE TO BE MONEY?`

segments.voice: Sadaqah is voluntary giving, beyond zakat, the yearly alms that are required. Yusuf's view first. In Sahih al-Bukhari, the Prophet ﷺ says that every morning two angels come down. One says: God, give the one who spends a replacement. The other: God, bring loss to the one who holds back. Another report says to shield yourself from the Fire even with half a date. Half a date. The point is that something actually leaves your hand, every day, and the amount can be tiny. Giving that costs nothing can quietly become giving that never costs anything. Now Amira's view. In a report in Sahih Muslim, every joint of the body owes a charity each day, and the list that pays it is a fair word between two people, helping someone onto their mount, a kind word, each step toward prayer, moving something harmful out of the road. Money isn't on it. And here's where the two meet, in Bukhari. Someone asks the Prophet: what if a person has nothing to give? He answers: let him work with his hands, help himself and give. And if he can't? Help someone in need. And if he can't? Do good, and hold back from harm; that is his sadaqah. A ladder, with money near the top and no one left off it.
screen: `SADAQAH: GIVING BEYOND ZAKAT.` · `VIEW ONE: EVEN HALF A DATE.` · `VIEW TWO: EVERY JOINT OWES.` · `THE LADDER IN BUKHARI.` · then, large: `A LITTLE, DAILY.`

segments.voice: Find a cup, a jar, or an envelope, and put in one coin or one small bill if you have one, or a folded note naming one thing you'll do for someone tomorrow. Set it somewhere you'll see it every morning. Then sit, and let the jar be the first thing in the day's frame.
screen: `A CUP, A JAR, AN ENVELOPE.` · `ONE COIN, OR ONE NOTE.` · `WHERE YOU'LL SEE IT.`

segments.voice: Daily giving: sadaqah given every day, as little as half a date, and when there's no money, the work of your hands and the harm you hold back.
Keep it in your pocket: a little, daily, from the jar or from your hands. Ten of fourteen, given.

howItsDone: Some Muslim families keep a sadaqah box or jar at home and add a little each day, giving the contents to a mosque, a food bank or a neighbor in need; others give through daily acts of help when money is short. Zakat, the required yearly alms, is reckoned separately.

fork.setup: you've always heard that any kindness counts as sadaqah, so money doesn't matter. state the money view at its strongest.
options: money is the only real charity; kind words are just manners.
giving that never costs anything can stop costing you; even half a date makes something actually leave your hand.
kindness counts only if it's done for a stranger, never for family.
fork.reveal: the money view's best case: the angels pray for the one who spends, and half a date counts. the other view's best case: every joint owes a charity, paid in good deeds. Bukhari's ladder holds both.

chat.says: dad says daily sadaqah = money. i'm broke till payday. does my pantry shift count or not
options: It counts. No money, then the work of your hands: that's the ladder in Bukhari.
It doesn't. Only money counts, so skip it until payday and then give double.
Money never matters. Cash is just for show; only good deeds really count.
chat.meaning: Bukhari's ladder: give if you can; if not, work and help; if not, do good and hold back from harm. Yusuf's half-a-date view holds when payday comes.

notes: Debate shape: Yusuf's view (sadaqah should include money daily, even a little: Bukhari 1442, 1417) and Amira's (every good deed is sadaqah: Muslim 1009), joined by the ladder in Bukhari 1445. Confirm both are fairly stated as views held within the tradition.
'Zakat, the yearly alms' is the standard description (due after a lunar year on qualifying wealth); no amounts given.
Hadith numbers Bukhari 1442, 1417, 1445 (also 6022) and Muslim 1009 (also Bukhari 2989); confirm. Muslim 1009's list is abridged.
